references.text: The Passover lamb was to be eaten with unleavened bread, and nothing should remain until morning - this is the original Passover regulation that Exodus 34:25 refers back to.
A nearly identical formulation about not offering blood together with leavened bread, and that the fat from the festival sacrifice must not remain until morning.
The prohibition against leavened bread during the Feast of Unleavened Bread, which is linked to the Passover celebration.
Reiteration of the prohibition against eating leavened bread during Passover, and that none of the meat should be left until the next morning.
Instructions regarding the Passover sacrifice and the blood that was smeared on the doorposts - the basis for זֶבַח חַג הַפָּסַח (the festival offering of Passover).
The Passover lamb was to be eaten with unleavened bread, and nothing should remain until morning.
Expands and confirms the theological principle that certain sacrificial meat must be consumed on the same day.
Confirms and specifies the particular rules of Passover about not leaving anything until morning.
Retelling of the same law confirming the connection between the prohibition of leavened bread and the timing of the sacrifice.
The original source of the rule; provides historical context for why the sacrifice must not be left until morning.
